It found pieces of the answer in print: the least number when balances are asked for and none is forbidden (Kiss, Łaba, Marshall and Somlai); bounds by Łaba and Marshall, by Malikiosis, and by Malikiosis and Kolountzakis; and the clocks of p·q hours (Lam and Leung, who credit de Bruijn; without repeats, Kiss, Malikiosis, Somlai and Vizer).   it is weak evidence that it is new, and the paper lists what was found.
why: Credits and cautions dropped. Paper, Section 1.2, has six works: the page leaves out Malikiosis's own paper (Forum Math. Sigma 2022; 'When q does not divide |A|, the bound p^e(p^k+q) of (a) follows in a few lines from a display in that proof', a derivation 'due to another instance, which read that paper for Noon'), de Bruijn ('Lam and Leung, who credit de Bruijn') and Kiss, Malikiosis, Somlai and Vizer (sets, n = 1). And the searcher's own cautions are gone: prior-art.md, section 7, 'one half (multisets, Phi_q not dividing A) looks like an easy and unrecorded exercise, part of it two lines from a 2025 theorem ... what may be new is the half with Phi_q | A' and '35 requests found none; that is not a survey'; section 8, 'Not tried: Google Scholar, MathSciNet, zbMATH'.

So much of what is known about tilings is stated in terms of patterns,
and proofs in that field keep needing bounds of the kind "a set that balances here and not there has at least
so many marks". The theorem below gives the best such bounds on its clocks when repeats are allowed; it settles nothing about tilings.
why: 'What is known about tilings is largely stated in terms of patterns' is wider than the paper's 'the conditions of Coven and Meyerowitz, and most of what is known about Fuglede's conjecture in cyclic groups, are stated in these terms'; a mathematician will think of Hajos, Sands and periodicity. And your note's list 'What this is and is not' has a caution that the page drops just where it is needed: 'Nothing here bears on the tiling theorems themselves; it says how sharp one of their lemmas is.' The criterion itself is true as worded (tested on every pair of sets, and of markings with repeats, on clocks of 4 to 12 hours).
